history.dynasty: Modern (no royal dynasty; built by marble industrialist Ashok Patni of RK Marbles)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - this is a Jain temple of the Digambara sect; keep-or-drop decision needed for the temples dataset. Built by Ashok Patni of RK Marbles with the blessings of Jain sage Muni Sudha Sagar (disciple of Acharya Shri Vidyasagar Ji Maharaj); construction began in 1994-95 on the Aravalli hills beside NH-8 on the outskirts of Ajmer (about 7-9 km from the city centre). The main temple has a large idol of Guru Adinath (Rishabhanatha) on its first floor, and 24 miniature temples for the 24 Tirthankaras line up on the hills above; in 2002 the largest-ever ashta-dhatu statues were installed in the complex. The project was estimated at around Rs 50 crore but reportedly cost close to Rs 100 crore. It is an important pilgrimage site for Digambara Jains and a noted Ajmer tourist attraction.

name: Nareli Jain Temple
town: Ajmer (temple is at Nareli village, about 7-9 km from the city centre)
town_description: Ajmer, in central Rajasthan, is one of the state's oldest cities - founded by Chauhan king Ajaypal, seat of the Chauhan dynasty, home to the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, Taragarh Fort, Ana Sagar lake and the Jain pilgrimage centre of Soniji Ki Nasiyan. It is a major rail junction and a gateway to the pilgrimage town of Pushkar, 15 km away.
